reviews.one_line_contribution: A pre-registered measurement of how much of a retrieved-experience bank's gain is absorbed by an instruction optimized on the same training episodes, separated from the ceiling effect that any accuracy-matched but episode-content-free instruction would also produce, using a 'headroom curve' of information-free instructions, a train-half provenance crossover with a planted half-specific positive control, and a token-matched compiled-bank arm.
reviews.closest_prior_work: EvoAgentBench (2607.05202) is the live threat: it already runs ReasoningBank, Memento and GEPA on the same 528/267 training trajectories across three backbones including Qwen3.5-27B, and reports GEPA within a couple of points of ReasoningBank (+1.2 vs +3.6) with no automatic method positive in every cell. That table already licenses this paper's practical takeaway ('the optimizer is a comparable container, and neither is reliable'), so the marginal contribution is the decomposition, not the finding. The proposal correctly identifies what EvoAgentBench lacks - combined I1xM cells, token matching, paired statistics, a compiled arm, provenance - and those absences are real. MIPROv2 (2406.11695) is the second threat and is the name a reviewer will say first: instruction-only vs demonstration-only vs joint on one training set is exactly the two-container ablation, and its recurring finding that the split is task-dependent pre-empts the qualitative answer here. A compounding weakness: Risk 14 refuses to re-measure any published number, so the study audits an evaluation template using its own re-implemented ExpeL/ReasoningBank banks. The track brief says a measurement contribution 'needs to overturn or qualify specific existing results to be interesting'; as written this paper qualifies no published result, only its own bank.
reviews.strongest_objection: The primary endpoint's identification assumption is false as stated and untested. Delta_abs = g_H(l1) - g(I1_ab, B_ab) treats memory's marginal gain as a function of no-memory accuracy alone, estimated from only three non-baseline points that are not even the same kind of intervention: H1 (an evidence-citation line), H2 ('decompose, search each, verify'), and I0+3, which is not an instruction at all but a search-budget increase that plausibly substitutes for memory through an entirely different channel (fewer wasted calls rather than better priors). Two prompts at equal aggregate accuracy leave different residual unsolved sets, and memory's marginal gain depends on the composition of that residual, not its size - so g_H(l1) is not the counterfactual gain of a non-absorbing instruction at level l1, and a positive Delta_abs is equally consistent with GEPA's prompt merely shifting which instances remain unsolved, with no episode content absorbed. Worse, the between-instruction scatter of g at matched level is exactly the null distribution Delta_abs must beat, and with three points at SE ~0.8-1.15pt each it cannot be estimated. The pre-registered primary comparator is anyway the single nearest member I_H*, so the 'curve' is decoration and the confirmatory test is a two-point contrast between one hand-picked generic instruction and one optimized instruction. The arithmetic then makes it worse: the 2pt claim threshold sits below the proposal's own stated MDE of 2.9pt and at the ~2pt treatment-free floor it computes in Measurement (c), and no null replicate of Delta_abs itself exists (cell 10 replicates only g at I0). A 2pt Delta_abs therefore cannot clear the rule 'no effect is claimed unless it exceeds both its test threshold and the 95th percentile of the relevant floor' - the confirmatory result is designed to be inconclusive at its own threshold.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Expand the information-free family to at least six members spanning the accuracy range, and either drop I0+3 from the curve or model it separately, since a budget change is not an instruction and its interaction with memory is mechanistically different; then report the residual scatter of g around the fitted curve and use that scatter - not sampling SE alone - as the null distribution for Delta_abs. (2) Add a genuine null replicate of the primary endpoint: compute Delta_abs between two information-free instructions that land at matched levels, where the true value is zero, at n=1,500; without this the 2pt threshold is uncalibrated. (3) Add an instance-composition diagnostic to the paired analysis - report the Jaccard overlap of the solved sets of I_H* and I1_ab and re-express Delta_abs conditional on the shared residual set - so the reader can see whether level-matching also matched what was left to fix. (4) Promote cell 18 (D_opt and the MIPROv2-style joint J) from Tier 1 to Tier 0 and raise the claim threshold above the achieved MDE, or buy power with more optimizer seeds rather than more Tier-1 cells. (5) Recover at least one published number: run the screened bank under one target paper's own reported setting, even at reduced n, so the audit attaches to a real claim rather than only to a self-built bank.
reviews.missing_baseline: The optimized static-demonstration container as a must-ship arm. D_opt and the MIPROv2-style joint instruction+demonstration prompt J are cell 18, sit at Tier 1, and are third in the Tier-1 cut order - so the most likely published outcome has them absent. The title asserts memory is 'just an un-optimized prompt', but a retrieved-experience bank is shaped like the demonstration slot, and instruction-only GEPA is not that slot's representative; MIPROv2 already reports that the instruction/demonstration split is task-dependent, which is precisely the alternative explanation this design leaves open. If J x M0 matches or beats I1_ab x M_ab, the paper's finding is about the demonstration container, not about memory being redundant with instructions, and the headline has to change. A second, cheaper omission: no compute-matched sampling baseline (self-consistency / best-of-n at memory's token budget) - I0+3 raises search calls only, so 'spend memory's budget elsewhere' is tested through one channel out of two.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is unusually strong for a proposal and should be credited: dated scans (2026-09-03, prior 2026-08-21), stated query counts and channels, by-id verification for 54 IDs, a committed scan record with a SHA256 for the closest work's extracted text, an explicit retraction of v2's overclaim that 'no published work uses one as the control for the other', and a correction of a web snippet that had misreported ReasoningBank's Qwen gain as +7 against the PDF's +3.6. I know of no preprint that already makes the specific Delta_abs claim - absorption measured against a level-matched information-free control - and EvoAgentBench, the nearest, is handled honestly rather than hidden. Three real weaknesses. First, arXiv is unreachable from the node, so every citation rests on web-search snippets plus one PI-supplied PDF; the entire novelty argument against the closest work is a single-source chain with no independent channel, which is the same failure mode that produced v2's false retractions. Second, arXiv 2608.14036 - the skills-vs-Workflow-Memory paper, i.e. the single most likely place a compiled-block-vs-live-retrieval comparison already exists - has an unopened appendix that is merely 'flagged'; that is the collision that would gut prediction 4 and cell 9, and it is unchecked. Third, and most damaging, the proposal admits that the design primitive it is most proud of - a held-out-episode provenance crossover asking whether an optimizer's gain is specific to the episodes it saw - was never searched for and is only on the pre-freeze list. Novelty for the crossover instrument is therefore currently unestablished by the proposal's own account, and the contamination / data-attribution literature is a plausible place for it to already live.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A pre-registered measurement of how much of a retrieved-experience memory bank's benefit is absorbed by an instruction that a reflective optimizer (GEPA) wrote from the same 800 training episodes, with the genuinely new instrument being the 'headroom curve' — a family of information-free instructions (H1 evidence-citation, H2 decompose-and-verify, I0+3 extra search budget) used to subtract off the ceiling effect that any accuracy-raising prompt would produce, so that the residual Delta_abs can be read as absorption rather than as a better baseline.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two, and together they squeeze the contribution. (1) MIPROv2 (2406.11695): the instruction-only vs demonstration-only vs joint ablation on one training set IS the two-container question, and its recurring finding that the split is task-dependent already predicts the proposal's likely answer. The proposal's honest reply — retrieval, distillation, a held-out-episode crossover and token matching are added — is a delta of controls, not of question. (2) EvoAgentBench (2607.05202) as described: Vanilla / Memento / ReasoningBank / GEPA on shared 528/267 trajectories, and on Qwen3.5-27B — an in-scope candidate agent here — GEPA +1.2 vs ReasoningBank +3.6, with GEPA the strongest automatic method on Gemma-4-31B at +5.7. The qualitative headline 'a prompt optimizer on the same episodes gets you roughly what the memory bank gets you, on 27-31B models' is therefore already in the literature. What survives is narrower than the title implies: the combined cell I1xM_ab, the level-matched headroom control, the compiled block C_ab at matched tokens, and paired statistics. That is a worthwhile measurement paper but not a new claim about the world, and a reviewer who has read EvoAgentBench will say so.
reviews.strongest_objection: The primary confirmatory endpoint is not identified by the design that is supposed to identify it. Delta_abs = g_H(l1) - g(I1_ab, B_ab) requires that memory's gain depends on the instruction ONLY through the no-memory accuracy level — a one-dimensional headroom assumption anchored on three points, one of which (I0+3) is not an instruction at all but a tool-budget change, and which the proposal itself concedes may require extrapolating past the family's range because a 350-rollout GEPA instruction will plausibly outrun a one-line 'cite your evidence' prompt. Two prompts at equal no-memory accuracy can differ enormously in how usable retrieved items are (H2's decompose-and-verify reshapes the trajectory distribution; I0+3 changes it via search, not context), so a positive Delta_abs is equally consistent with 'GEPA wrote a better GENERIC procedural instruction than H1/H2' — nothing absorbed from any episode. The design's only probe that could discriminate this is Delta_info, and Falsifiable Prediction 2 pre-registers Delta_info within [-1,+1]pt in E1 and calls that outcome 'generic absorption, reported as such, not a failure.' That is circular: the mechanism probe is pre-declared to return the uninformative value, and the uninformative value is then read as confirmation. Compounding it, the planted control B_a+proc10 is written from gold documents and certifies sensitivity only to near-oracle half-specific items at ~15-30pt, not to the 1-2pt natural content whose absence the null is meant to license (Risk 12 admits this, then the interpretation rule ignores it). Second-order but real: the claim threshold is 2pt while the stated MDE is <=2.9pt and the measured treatment-free floor is ~2pt at n=1,500 — the headline effect is the size of the study's own noise.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Four concrete changes, none of which require more than a modest budget increase. (1) Make the headroom family an actual curve: 5-6 information-free instructions chosen on S_dev2 to BRACKET acc(I1_ab x M0) from both sides, with the pre-registration forbidding extrapolation; and validate the one-dimensional assumption directly by showing that two family members at matched levels give matched g — if they do not, Delta_abs is not interpretable and the paper should say so before unblinding. (2) Add the bank re-distilled under the optimized instruction (see missing_baseline) so that Delta_abs is not confounded with trajectory-distribution mismatch. (3) Promote cell 12 (I1a x M0, I1b x M0) and cell 19 (I3 length control) from Tier 1 to Tier 0: the Tier-0 confirmatory family F-B is uninterpretable without per-half M0 levels (if neither own nor other bank beats M0 at I1a, Delta_info ~ 0 says nothing, planted control or not), and the whole content-vs-length story rests on I3, which the contingency order currently allows to be cut. (4) Make the confirmatory environment one with recurring procedural structure. Running the substitution test primarily in E1 (BM25 multi-hop QA over HotpotQA/MuSiQue/2Wiki) tests it where procedural memory is least likely to have anything to absorb; if memory is absorbable there, the memory community will answer that they never claimed gains there. E2 or a web/tool agent should carry the confirmatory result, with E1 as replication.
reviews.missing_baseline: A bank re-distilled from episodes generated UNDER the optimized instruction (call it B_ab | I1). As written, screening stage S1 generates the 800-episode training pool with bare I0, so every bank item is a lesson extracted from I0-shaped trajectories, and cell 3 then injects those items into an agent running I1_ab. If memory's gain shrinks at I1_ab, the most mundane explanation available to a reviewer is not absorption and not headroom but distribution mismatch: the bank's procedures no longer describe what the optimized agent does. I2_ab runs the opposite coupling (optimizer sees the bank) and does not cover this. Without B_ab | I1 the paper is auditing others for a confound of exactly the kind it leaves in its own primary cell. Secondary omission: a token-matched LONG hand-written instruction is only I3 at Tier 1 and is cuttable, yet the 'content not length' reading of Delta_abs depends on it.
reviews.preprint_collision: Above average as a process and it should be credited: dated re-scan (2026-09-03 over 2026-08-21), 15 HF queries, 244 papers, by-id verification of 54 IDs, a committed scan record with SHA256s, and — rare and to its credit — an explicit retraction of v2's claim that 'no published work uses one as the control for the other' after finding EvoAgentBench (2607.05202). But three things keep it from being a clean pass. First, the channel is demonstrably unreliable by the proposal's own admission: arXiv is unreachable from the node, verification runs through web-search snippets, and the August scan produced five false negatives (ActMem, MAS-PromptBench, TERMS-Bench, MemAPO, StructMemEval all exist) — a searcher with that false-negative rate cannot support a strong novelty claim, and the closest work is known only through a PDF supplied by the PI rather than a fetched source. Second, the check itself concedes the design primitive has never been searched: item (2) of the pre-freeze list is a targeted search for held-out-episode / data-provenance crossovers in prompt optimization and contamination work, i.e. the crossover that certifies the specificity probe is claimed novel without ever having been looked for. Own-vs-other-split transfer is a standard memorization/contamination move, and a collision there is likely. Third, the most damaging collision is not a hidden preprint but the one already cited: if EvoAgentBench really reports GEPA +1.2 vs ReasoningBank +3.6 on Qwen3.5-27B and GEPA +5.7 as the best automatic method on Gemma-4-31B, then 'an optimizer on the same episodes rivals the memory bank' is published, and this proposal is the careful follow-up measurement rather than the discovery. The residual-risk paragraph naming ICLR 2027 non-public submissions and NeurIPS 2026 camera-readies is realistic, and the re-scan commitment is the right mitigation, but as of the submitted text novelty rests on a search that has not covered one of the two design primitives.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A pre-registered paired measurement of how much of a retrieved procedural-experience bank's benefit survives once the instruction slot is filled by a GEPA-optimized prompt trained on the same 800 episodes, with a family of information-free instructions (H1 evidence-citation, H2 decompose-and-verify, I0+3 extra search budget) used as a level-matched control so that the drop can be attributed to absorption rather than to a ceiling effect; secondary contributions are an own-bank/other-bank provenance crossover with a planted half-specific positive control, and a token-matched compiled block C_ab tested against live retrieval on top of the optimized instruction.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two, in different ways. (a) MIPROv2 (2406.11695) already runs the two-container ablation — instruction-only vs demonstration-only vs joint, optimized on one training set — and already reports that the split is task-dependent. The proposal concedes this and correctly notes MIPROv2 does not retrieve, distill, hold episodes out across containers, or token-match; but a reviewer will say the conceptual claim (instructions and demonstrations are substitutable containers for the same training signal, in proportions that vary by task) is MIPROv2's finding, and this proposal supplies a query-conditioned read and better statistics rather than a new claim. (b) EvoAgentBench (cited as 2607.05202) is the empirical threat: it already places ReasoningBank and GEPA on the same 528/267 trajectories and on Qwen3.5-27B, one of this proposal's own candidate agents, reporting +3.6 vs +1.2. The proposal's audit of it is honest and the remaining delta is real — no combined optimizer-plus-memory cell, no token matching, no compiled arm, no paired statistics — but that delta is an ablation-grade contribution layered onto an existing table, not a new object of study. I note I cannot independently verify EvoAgentBench, which is a 2026-07 preprint read from a PI-supplied PDF; if its appendix contains any GEPA+memory cell, the contribution collapses to the headroom control alone.
reviews.strongest_objection: The confirmatory endpoint is not identified. Delta_abs = g_H(l1) - g(I1_ab, B_ab) assumes memory's gain is a function of no-memory accuracy level alone, so that any instruction at level l1 that carries no episode content predicts what memory should have added. The information-free family cannot support that assumption: H2 ('decompose the question into sub-questions, search each, and verify before finishing') is content-identical to the modal ExpeL/ReasoningBank insight for multi-hop QA, so g(H2, B_ab) is depressed by content overlap; I0+3 is a pure tool-budget change that alters how much evidence is already in context and therefore changes memory's marginal value through a completely different channel; I0 is the un-optimized scaffold. These three points do not lie on one curve indexed by accuracy, and the proposal's own Risk 4 concedes H2's overlap while calling it 'the point'. Worse, the pre-registered primary comparator is not the interpolated curve but the single family member I_H* nearest l1 — and I_H* is selected on S_dev2 at n=300 where the paired gain has SE ~2.4pt by the proposal's own arithmetic. So the headline number depends on which of three qualitatively different one-liners happens, within noise, to land nearest wherever GEPA's accuracy falls; if it is H2 the estimate is biased conservative, if it is I0+3 it is biased anti-conservative, and nothing in the design distinguishes these. The proposal also allows l1 to fall outside the family's range, in which case the confirmatory endpoint is an extrapolation 'reported as a limitation' — a confirmatory endpoint that may be an extrapolation off a three-point curve is not confirmatory. Compounding this, the claim threshold (2pt) sits below the stated MDE (<=2.9pt) and below the treatment-free null floor the proposal itself expects (~2pt at n=1,500), and the G1/G2/G7' gate chain — each with modest power at n=300, where they compute that a true 1pt effect passes G1 only ~10% of the time — makes 'no pairing clears the gates, publish the memory-null report' the modal outcome by the design's own numbers. The likeliest reading of this submission is a rigorous study that never gets to test its title.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Replace the three-point information-free family with a genuine level control that varies one thing monotonically — e.g. search budget swept over 6, 8, 11, 14 calls, or partial adoption of I1_ab's edits — so g_H(l) is estimated at five or more levels that bracket l1, fit with a slope and CI that is propagated into SE(Delta_abs) instead of picking one nearest neighbour on a 300-instance dev sample; keep H1/H2 as secondary points, not as the primary comparator. 2) Add the on-policy bank arm named in missing_baseline. 3) Abandon random 400/400 halves for the crossover: random halves of one pool are exchangeable by construction, the proposal admits Delta_info is expected to be zero in E1, and cells 5/6/11/12/13 spend roughly 24,000 Tier-0 episodes confirming a foregone conclusion. Split instead by structure — bridge vs comparison questions and source dataset in E1, the six ALFWorld task types in E2 — so provenance has something to carry and a null is informative. 4) Make E2 the confirmatory environment rather than a Tier-1 reduced-budget replication: tool-augmented multi-hop QA over a fixed corpus is the domain where procedural memory has least to teach (the whole lesson is roughly H2), so a demonstration of absorption there is close to rigged and least interesting; recurring-subroutine environments are where the answer matters, and the proposal's own Prediction 2 concedes this. 5) Either raise n or move the claim threshold above the MDE and the 95th-percentile null floor, so a pass is not defined at an effect size the instrument cannot resolve. 6) Elevate cell 8 (I2_ab, the instruction co-optimized with the bank) from a 2-seed secondary to a primary arm: the track asks about coupling between a self-editing memory and an optimizer, and this proposal explicitly refuses self-editing (Risk 13) and demotes the only coupling cell — it answers a substitution question the track did not pose while leaving the track's named question to a secondary endpoint.
reviews.missing_baseline: An on-policy bank: a bank B^{I1} distilled from training episodes generated under I1_ab (or under each information-free instruction), retrieved at that same instruction. As written, every bank is distilled from episodes the agent ran under bare I0 (screening stage S1: 'run bare I0 on the 800-episode training pool (bank-gen)'), so at I1_ab the bank is off-policy: its INSIGHT/PROCEDURE/OUTCOME items describe traces produced by a different policy with a different step structure and output style. Memory's gain shrinking at I1_ab is then equally explained by bank staleness as by the instruction having absorbed the information, and the two are not separated anywhere in the 23-cell grid. H1/H2/I0+3 only partially control for this, since a one-line handwritten addition perturbs the policy far less than an evolved GEPA instruction, so the policy-shift magnitude is not matched along the headroom curve — which means the confound is largest exactly at the point the primary endpoint is evaluated. Cell 8 (I2_ab) does not cover it: it lets the optimizer see the bank, but the bank is still I0-derived. A secondary omission: an instruction optimized at matched rollout budget on episodes disjoint from the bank's source pool at full data — cell 5 does this only at 400-episode halves, so the title's load-bearing phrase 'optimized on the same episodes' is never tested at the scale the primary endpoint uses.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is well above the norm and should be credited: it is dated (2026-09-03, prior 2026-08-21), states its channels and counts (15 HuggingFace queries, 244 papers, 54 by-id verifications), commits raw scan records with SHA256s, explicitly withdraws v2's sentence that no published work uses one method as the control for the other, and reinstates five citations a previous round had wrongly retracted with a stated procedural rule. Naming EvoAgentBench (2607.05202) as a near-collision and enumerating what it does and does not contain is exactly the right move. Three real weaknesses remain. First, arXiv is unreachable from the node, so nearly every post-2026 ID rests on web-search snippets — and the check itself records that a snippet misreported ReasoningBank's Qwen gain as +7 against the PDF's +3.6. That is direct evidence the verification channel is unreliable, yet the entire related-work map and the motivating numbers rest on it, and the one paper checked properly was checked from a PDF supplied by the PI rather than obtained independently. Second, the appendix of 2608.14036 (skills vs Workflow Memory) is admittedly unopened and is precisely where a token-matched compiled-block-versus-retrieval comparison would live — i.e. where Prediction 4, the compile-once result, would already be scooped; deferring that to a 'pre-freeze re-scan' means the compile contribution's novelty is currently unestablished, not merely unconfirmed. Third, and most telling, the proposal states that the design primitive it leans on hardest — a held-out-episode provenance crossover asking whether an optimizer's gain is specific to the episodes it saw — has never been searched at all and is item (2) on the re-scan list. A novelty claim for the crossover therefore has no search behind it. Note also that I cannot verify any of the 26xx-series IDs myself; I am judging the check's method and self-consistency, not the existence of the papers.
